Changed since your last export: you now only place 10 things, not 16. Each paired limb (thigh, shin, foot, upper arm, forearm, hand) used to have a separate draggable "near" and "far" copy for the side-view depth trick — that's what was going wrong: once the two copies drifted apart it stopped reading as depth and started reading as duplicate/extra limbs, and it's also what exposed a joint-connector nub near the hip. Now you only place the near copy of each; the far copy is computed automatically as a small fixed offset behind it (tune how big that gap looks with the two sliders below the stage) and isn't draggable or selectable — so it can't drift apart anymore. If you paste your old exported JSON into the Load box, the old separately-placed far copies are dropped automatically and your near placements (including any rotation you dialed in) carry over as-is. Click a part on the left to drop it on stage. Click any piece to select it (drag to move, arrow keys nudge 1px / shift+arrow 10px), then rotate/resize/mirror it from the right-hand panel. Use the Layers list to push one piece in front of or behind a specific neighbor. Use Fullscreen plus the zoom slider for more precise dragging. When it looks right, hit Export layout and send me back the JSON.
